question: What is the primary goal of closing a skin laceration with sutures?

options.A: To prevent the need for tetanus shots
options.B: To eliminate all local blood supply

explanation: Bringing clean wound edges together speeds up primary intention healing and reduces scarring. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why is the time elapsed since the injury important when deciding to suture?

options.A: Suture threads dissolve faster in older wounds
options.B: Skin loses all its natural elasticity overnight
options.C: Bacterial multiplication increases significantly after twelve hours
options.D: Local anesthesia stops working after six hours have passed

explanation: Wounds older than twelve hours carry a much higher risk of trapping bacteria inside if closed immediately. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h1)

question: What check must always happen distal to a limb laceration before suturing?
explanation: Checking movement, feeling, and blood flow below the injury ensures nerves and vessels are intact. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h2)

question: When is a tetanus booster usually indicated for a laceration injury?

options.A: If the patient has never experienced a fever before
options.B: Every time any patient receives a single skin stitch
options.C: When the last dose was over five to ten years ago
options.D: Only when the wound was caused by a clean kitchen knife

explanation: Outdated tetanus immunity leaves the patient vulnerable to infection, making vaccination status vital during assessment. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h2)

question: Where should you NEVER use a local anesthetic containing epinephrine?
explanation: Epinephrine constricts blood vessels so severely in end-artery digits that it can cause tissue death. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of adding epinephrine to a local anesthetic solution?

options.A: It makes the suture needle slide through skin much faster
options.B: It completely sterilizes the local wound area
options.C: It reduces bleeding and extends anesthesia duration
options.D: It eliminates the need for any physical cleaning

explanation: Vasoconstriction keeps the drug local longer and gives a clearer, bloodless field to work in. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the most effective method for reducing bacteria inside an open wound?
explanation: Physical flushing with sterile saline washes away loose bacteria and microscopic particles effectively. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why should harsh chemical antiseptics be kept out of an open wound bed?

options.A: They change the color of the patient's skin permanently
options.B: They damage healthy tissue and delay healing
options.C: They cause the suture thread to break down instantly
options.D: They immediately dissolve the local anesthetic drug

explanation: Toxic chemicals harm host cells just as much as bacteria, impairing the natural repair process. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which suture material is typically used for closing the outer skin layer?
explanation: Nylon is a strong non-absorbable material ideal for outer skin where it will later be removed. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h5)

question: Where on the suture needle should the needle holder be clamped?

options.A: At the very end of the trailing thread
options.B: One-third to halfway from the swaged end
options.C: Directly in the exact middle of the curve
options.D: Right at the sharp tip of the needle

explanation: Clamping at this point provides stability and prevents the needle from bending during tissue entry. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h5)

question: At what angle should the suture needle enter the skin surface?
explanation: Entering perpendicular to the skin surface allows the curved needle to rotate smoothly through the tissue. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main advantage of using simple interrupted sutures?

options.A: If one stitch fails or gets infected, the others remain intact
options.B: They eliminate the need for any local numbing agents
options.C: They take half the time to complete compared to staples
options.D: They never leave any marks or scarring on the skin

explanation: Because every single knot is tied separately, a single failure does not compromise the whole wound. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h6)

question: What substance is often recommended to keep a fresh suture line moist?
explanation: Keeping a wound moist with petroleum jelly prevents heavy scab formation and helps minimize scarring. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why should patients avoid soaking a freshly sutured wound in water?

options.A: It softens the tissue and increases infection risk
options.B: Water instantly dissolves the non-absorbable nylon
options.C: Soaking causes the skin edges to fuse together too fast
options.D: Moisture prevents the local anesthesia from wearing off

explanation: Prolonged water immersion can introduce bacteria and macerate delicate healing skin edges. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which body area generally requires the shortest time before suture removal?
explanation: Facial skin heals rapidly due to excellent blood supply, and early removal prevents permanent track marks. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h8)

question: Why should you pull the cut suture thread toward the wound line during removal?

options.A: To keep the scissors from getting dull too quickly
options.B: To prevent pulling surface bacteria through the tissue tract
options.C: To ensure the patient feels less pulling sensation
options.D: To make the knot easier to grab with sterile forceps

explanation: Pulling away from the wound can pop the healing edges back open or drag contaminated surface thread through the deeper skin. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h8)

question: What is the most common adverse outcome following simple laceration repair?
explanation: Bacteria introduced during injury or procedural steps can multiply, making infection the leading complication. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h9)

question: Which of the following is NOT a classic sign of a localized wound infection?
explanation: Infection typically causes increased blood flow and inflammation, which feels warm or hot to the touch rather than cool. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h9)
